question:
Site question from the owner of papertrades.ai (Sat Oct 31, 2 a.m. ET; day 4 of 32). NOT a trading turn; nothing in your books changes. The owner wants all three AIs (Claude, Gemini, ChatGPT) to work this out together. Be concrete and honest; disagree where you disagree.

A REVIEWER (Gemini, in a separate chat) SAID: to reach a 10/10 the platform needs (1) higher execution speed for real-time alerts, (2) more granular historical data for backtesting, and (3) deeper analytics of each model's performance under different market conditions.

FACTS FROM OUR OWN DATA (Claude measured them just now):
- Each trade, bet and result is posted to Telegram and Discord in the same run that fills it (seconds after the fill). The decision cadence is the limit: Gemini and ChatGPT checked in 45 times in the last 36 hours (never more than 90 minutes apart); Claude runs hourly plus every 30 minutes in US market hours plus market opens and closes. GitHub's scheduled timer is unreliable (a ':13' run started anywhere from :57 to :37, and some hours had no scheduled run), but Claude's runs dispatch the rivals' check-ins, so no gaps appeared.
- Stops and targets are filled by the race runner at every run (about every 30 to 60 minutes), at the live price then.
- Stored today: every trade and bet with time, price, size and reason; each AI's value per race at every check-in (about 2,400 points so far); 24-hour price series for held assets and longer daily/weekly history for 20 symbols; nightly SHA-256 fingerprint of the full record. Only 3.5 days of race data exist.

CLAUDE'S PROPOSALS (rate each: IMPACT 1-10 for trust and audience, EFFORT low/medium/high, DO NOW / LATER / SKIP, one line why; say if the version is wrong):
A1. Publish the speed honestly on Rules & Audit: for each AI, check-ins in the last 24 hours, the longest gap, and the median delay from fill to Telegram post (measured, not claimed).
A2. Faster stops: a light "stops-only" runner every 10 to 15 minutes in market hours for all three AIs equally (no model call, so it is cheap); decisions stay on the current schedule.
A3. More frequent decision check-ins (every 15 minutes) for all three: only if Claude's runs can match, otherwise it is unfair. Claude's view: LATER (cost and fairness).
B1. A "Data" page: download everything (every trade, bet, result, value per race at every check-in, price series), per AI and race, as CSV and JSON, with the fingerprint, so anyone can run their own analysis or backtest.
B2. A public read-only JSON endpoint (the same files, stable URLs, documented) so developers can build on it.
C1. "Under different conditions": tag each period by market condition (S&P up or down day, a volatility-spike day, a big crypto move, a scheduled-event day such as a Fed decision or big earnings) and show each AI's average result per condition, with the number of periods and a clear "too early to judge" until there are enough.
C2. Decision-quality stats per AI and race: win rate, average win vs average loss, average holding time, how often stops were hit, and whether the rivals' grades predicted the results (a grade-vs-outcome table).
Claude's order: B1, C2, A1, C1, A2, B2, A3.

PLEASE ANSWER IN EXACTLY THIS FORMAT (short):
A1: IMPACT <n> · EFFORT <x> · <DO NOW|LATER|SKIP>: <why / change>
A2: ...
A3: ...
B1: ...
B2: ...
C1: ...
C2: ...
YOUR ORDER (the first 4):
MISSING (one idea that would matter more than these, or "nothing"):

chatgpt.answer:
A1: IMPACT 9 · EFFORT low · DO NOW: correct version; measured latency/gaps build trust fast.
A2: IMPACT 7 · EFFORT medium · DO NOW: improves stop/target fairness if identical for all AIs and fully logged.
A3: IMPACT 4 · EFFORT high · LATER: not worth cost/fairness risk until Claude can match cadence.
B1: IMPACT 10 · EFFORT medium · DO NOW: strongest trust move; lets outsiders verify everything.
B2: IMPACT 7 · EFFORT medium · LATER: valuable after B1 files/format are stable.
C1: IMPACT 6 · EFFORT medium · LATER: useful framing, but 3.5 days is too little; show “too early.”
C2: IMPACT 9 · EFFORT medium · DO NOW: best near-term analytics; disclose small sample sizes.
YOUR ORDER (the first 4): B1, A1, C2, A2
MISSING: Public runner/data-freshness status page showing last successful run, failed runs, and current stale-data warnings.

gemini.answer:
A1: IMPACT 7 · EFFORT low · DO NOW: Transparency builds trust immediately and counters false expectations of ultra-low latency execution.
A2: IMPACT 8 · EFFORT medium · DO NOW: Missing a stop because of a 45-minute scheduler gap ruins trade fidelity; a light script fixes this without adding AI API costs.
A3: IMPACT 3 · EFFORT high · SKIP: GitHub cron is too unreliable for 15-minute syncs, and the AI cost-to-signal ratio isn't worth it for daily/swing trading.
B1: IMPACT 9 · EFFORT medium · DO NOW: The ultimate answer to "granular data"; lets reviewers backtest on their own terms and proves we hide nothing.
B2: IMPACT 5 · EFFORT medium · LATER: B1's static file downloads solve the immediate need; a live API is overkill for Day 4.
C1: IMPACT 6 · EFFORT medium · LATER: With only 3.5 days of data, macro tagging is meaningless right now; wait until mid-November to build this out.
C2: IMPACT 9 · EFFORT low · DO NOW: Standard trading metrics (win rate, average win/loss) are table stakes for a trading competition and easily calculated from existing logs.

YOUR ORDER: B1, C2, A2, A1

MISSING: Visual price charts with each AI's entry, exit, and stop points overlaid. Seeing exactly *where* an AI traded on a chart provides far better, more intuitive analytics on "market conditions" than textual data tagging.
